name: OPA627 / OPA637
tagline: Burr-Brown's Difet JFET single, long the 'king' of op-amp rolling: detailed, smooth, pA bias, 4.5 nV/√Hz.

lineage.note: Tucson, AZ; Difet successor to the OPA111. Launch c. 1989; PSpice models dated October 1990.
SBOS165 from 2000; Rev A 2015, B 2024, C 2025. PSpice SBOM099/SBOC118, SBOM101/SBOC119.
Reportedly sells OPA627AM and DIP continuation stock via DigiKey Marketplace; unverified.

part_numbers.note: SOIC-8, A grade. 2024: 'will not be packaged for now'; TI suggests OPA828ID. Heavily faked.
New SOIC B grade (not Burr-Brown era); preview in Rev B, production in SBOS165C.
DIP-8, A/B grade (B: tighter offset, drift). AP obsolete per DigiKey; BP common remark target.
TO-99, A/B grade; only package with offset trim. TI said stock coming (2024); NRND unconfirmed.
TO-99, military temperature grade; very rare (Soomal). Date unknown.
Bare die; DigiKey hosts its datasheet. Orderable and doc numbers not captured.
SOIC-8, decompensated (G ≥ 5); OPA637 product folder active.
No evidence it exists; Rev C mentions only OPA627BU.
DIP-8, decompensated; presumed obsolete with the DIP line. Broker listings exist.
TO-99, decompensated. Genuine BM cans ¥250+ (Soomal); only pulled stock by 2021.

key_specs.value: 4.5 nV/√Hz (10 kHz; 1 kHz value not captured)

key_specs.condition: OPA627 figure from EDA library only

key_specs.value: 7.5 mA max per amp (~7–7.5 mA observed)

reputation.summary: The benchmark audiophile JFET single: the 'king' on English forums, 'legendary' in Japan. Soomal hears it warm-leaning with full mids, strong dynamics and space, resolving HF better than OPA111/OPA2107, and rates the OPA637 slightly higher. Leckerton notes blind tests show no clear win over cheaper parts like the AD8610.
typical_uses: DAC I/V and post-filter stages (HiFiMAN HM-901)
Headphone amp cards with BUF634 (HiFiMAN IEM, Minibox)
Line buffers, preamps, phono and high-impedance inputs
Op-amp rolling in sound cards and DACs via adapters
Photodiode transimpedance and instrumentation front ends
caveats: Single only; dual sockets need an adapter. Up to ~7.5 mA per amp means heat and battery drain.
OPA637 is unstable below a noise gain of about 5; never use it as a unity-gain buffer.
One of the most counterfeited audiophile op-amps; DIP versions are obsolete.
Current molded parts have pins 1/5 NC; offset trim works on TO-99 only.
Origin folklore (US > Taiwan > SE Asia) and grade differences are unmeasured; A/B grades reportedly inaudible.

counterfeit_notes: Heavily faked: ZeptoBars (2014) found an AD744 die in a $2.7 eBay 'OPA627'. Check Iq (~7–7.5 mA), slew, square waves; trim-pin tests fail on new parts. Cheap TO-99 OPA637BM and 'custom metal-can' parts are fake. Buy AU/BU authorized.

silicon_changes.summary: TI's 2024–2025 rewrite deleted 'Difet', added the OPA627BU and made molded trim pins NC. For the sister OPA132, TI cites a 'new FAB change and design'. This suggests new silicon under the same part numbers, but no PCN or OPA627-specific confirmation exists. Rev A was still cited in June 2022.
silicon_changes.identification: SBOS165B/C titled 'OPA6x7 Precision, High-Speed JFET'; molded pins 1/5 NC; OPA627BU only from 2024–2025. No PCN or date-code cut-over; BB-logo and pre-2024 parts keep working trim pins.

spec_deltas.after: NC; trim documented for TO-99 only (SBOS165B/C)
AU and BU (BU production data in Rev C, Jan 2025)

silicon_changes.audio_impact: Unknown; no before/after measurements. Pin 1/5 offset nulling is lost on new molded parts; Burr-Brown-era impressions may not carry over.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: medium: offset-trim circuits fail on new molded parts; Rev A to C electrical deltas not captured.
silicon_changes.verification: Rev B/C history, Difet deletion, BU production and NC pins confirmed; die change inferred from OPA132.

silicon_changes.summary: Temporary supply suspension of the OPA627AU during the 2024–2025 documentation (and likely silicon) change. TI named the OPA828ID as pin-to-pin replacement, a different SiGe JFET-input die. Status stayed active; BU and TO-can stock was expected in about two months.
silicon_changes.identification: Status active, but SOIC-8 AU temporarily not packaged (2024).

spec_deltas.after: Active, SOIC-8 temporarily not packaged (2024); OPA828ID suggested as replacement

silicon_changes.audio_impact: None to the silicon; the OPA828ID is a different die with different noise, bandwidth and bias.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: medium: AU supply interrupted; TI's suggested replacement is a different die.
silicon_changes.verification: E2E thread confirms AU active but unpackaged, OPA828ID suggested, BU/TO-can stock due.

silicon_changes.summary: Soomal (2016) ranks Taiwan-made parts second to US-made and ahead of SE Asian. Japanese sellers claim Burr-Brown-era parts use a different process rule and thicker bond wires. No vendor document, PCN or measurement supports this.
silicon_changes.identification: Collector folklore: Burr-Brown logo, pre-2000 date code, US or Taiwan origin.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low: same pinout and specs; 'vintage BB' listings attract remarked fakes.
silicon_changes.verification: No documentary support; kept as folklore.

revision_history.changes: Not a datasheet; proves the part existed by October 1990.
Introduced in plastic DIP and TO-99 (TI E2E 1393043). Reportedly in the 1990 Supplement 33b. PDS base inferred from PDS-998H.
SOIC (AU/BU) added; in the 1995 Burr-Brown IC Data Book. No standalone copy found.
'Printed in U.S.A. March, 1998' (Carnegie copy); PDIP, SOIC, TO-99. Letter H implies earlier editions A–G.
TI number after the acquisition, presumably Burr-Brown content; Rev C header says August 2000. Served c. 2004 at focus.ti.com.
TI format with ESD Ratings (HBM ±2500 V, CDM ±1000 V SOIC); still 'Difet', pins 1/5 Trim. Cited by TI models in June 2022.
Probably deleted Difet references, added OPA627BU preview, retitled 'OPA6x7'. Pins 1/5 NC (TO-99 trim only) in B or C.
OPA627BU from preview to production data; first-issue date now reads August 2000.

revision_chains.note: PDS-998 through PDS-998G not found as standalone sheets; 1990, 1995, 1998 databooks are the leads.
No copy of original or Rev B; OPA637 never had a separate sheet.

open_questions: Did Rev B or C make pins 1/5 NC and delete Difet? Does a PCN confirm a new die?
Electrical deltas SBOS165A to SBOS165C: e_n at 1 kHz, Vos, Ib, Iq and output current.
Current status of TO-99 AM/BM/SM and OPA637 TO-99 parts; does an OPA637BU exist?
OPA627-DIE orderable and doc number; any Rev D after January 2025?
Burr-Brown launch-year datasheet (c. 1989); confirm OPA627 16 MHz GBW and 7.5 mA max Iq.

claims_confirmed: SBOS165C current ('August 2000 – revised January 2025'); OPA627BU to production; Rev B April 2024 (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/opa627.pdf).
Current title 'OPA6x7 Precision, High-Speed JFET Operational Amplifiers' (https://www.ti.com/lit/gpn/OPA627 ; https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/opa637.pdf).
Revision history: Difet references deleted, OPA627BU preview added (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/opa627.pdf).
SBOS165A 'September 2000 – revised October 2015'; ESD HBM ±2500 V, CDM ±1000 V (https://www.mouser.com/datasheet/2/405/opa627-406898.pdf).
Molded trim pins now NC; trim on TO-99 only (https://www.diyaudio.com/community/threads/opa132-opa627-and-other-ti-bb-op-amps-no-longer-have-an-offset-trim-terminal.418419/).
TI attributes OPA132 NC trim pins to higher-precision manufacturing (https://e2e.ti.com/support/audio-group/audio/f/audio-forum/1517005/opa132-changed-opa132-pin-1-and-pin-8-from-offset-trim-to-nc).

2024: OPA627AU active but not packaged; OPA828ID suggested; BU/TO-can stock coming (https://e2e.ti.com/support/amplifiers-group/amplifiers/f/amplifiers-forum/1386960/opa627-is-the-opa627au-end-of-life).
OPA637: 80 MHz at G=10, 135 V/µs, active (https://www.ti.com/product/OPA637).
OPA627BU and OPA637AU orderable pages exist (https://www.ti.com/product/OPA627/part-details/OPA627BU ; https://www.ti.com/product/OPA637/part-details/OPA637AU).
4.5 nV/√Hz at 10 kHz, 55 V/µs, 100 µV, 0.8 µV/°C, 5 pA, ±4.5 to ±18 V (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/opa627.pdf).

Burr-Brown edition printed March 1998; dielectrically isolated NPN/PNP, laser-trimmed Difet (https://instrumentation.obs.carnegiescience.edu/ccd/parts/OPA627.pdf ; https://www.audiophonics.fr/images2/8434/opa627.pdf).
refuted_claims: 'TO-99 AM/BM/SM out of production' is contradicted: TI E2E 1386960 (2024) said TO-can stock was coming; status set to unclear.
'Revision A (April 2015)' is refuted: SBOS165A reads 'September 2000 – revised October 2015'.
'Metal-can fakes put a DIP die inside' misstates Soomal: some fakes put an ordinary PDIP chip inside a metal shell.
corrections: SBOS165C confirmed current; Rev B dated April 2024; OPA627BU to production in Rev C; symlink raised to high confidence.
Difet deletion, BU preview and 'OPA6x7' title confirmed; deletion and preview attributed to Rev B by inference.
NC pins 1/5 (TO-99 trim only) confirmed via diyAudio 418419; silicon-change confidence medium for documentation only.
OPA627AU active but temporarily unpackaged, OPA828ID suggested; OPA627AP confirmed obsolete.
OPA637 80 MHz (G=10) and 135 V/µs confirmed; product folder active.
Added copies: opa637 symlink, SBOS165A diagram, TI.com.cn viewer, Burr-Brown copies, Octopart OPA627BP, radiolocman OPA637, ciiva, OPA627-DIE.
Mouser, Cimarron and b-cdn copies freeze Rev A; Carnegie copy is the March 1998 Burr-Brown edition.
Pin 1–5 trim-resistance fake check flagged as invalid on new molded parts.
